headline: C92 (reports/c92_limit_category_retest.json) is RETRACTED. Its central method -- reading branch_misses to enumerate each engine arm's outcome -- is invalid, and C89's evidence table as originally written was wrong for the same reason (corrected in PR #1031).

the_method_error.what_i_did: parsed branch_misses with _miss_pairs and read the engine=[...] side as THE BRANCH'S component set, then asked whether the observed net appeared among the arms.
the_method_error.why_it_is_wrong: engine_transition_differential.py:1893 loops `for slot in ("p1","p2")` and does `ok = False; break` on the first failing slot. Each branch therefore contributes exactly ONE miss reason, for ONE slot. A branch whose p1 comparison failed reports nothing about p2.
the_method_error.the_artifact_it_produced: wherever a branch's miss named the OTHER slot, I computed a net of 0 for the slot I cared about and recorded an 'arm at net 0'. Those zero arms do not exist. Review replayed the true branch sets: 19000029/51 is [-118, -118] not [0, -118]; 19000052/36 is [-192, -192, -192] not [0, -211, -211]; 19000058/19 is [-14, -123, -123] not [0, 0, -123]; 19000074/27 is [-244, -116, -227] not [0, -116, -227].
the_method_error.the_6.25_percent_tell_i_missed: I read a 6.25% arm as a 'miss arm'. 6.25% is BASE_CRIT_CHANCE. Hidden Power is 100% accurate in gen3 -- there is no miss arm. That arm was the crit.
the_method_error.the_field_is_narrower_still: 'one slot per branch' understates it. differential:1934-1937 prints engine= as the ROLL-SCALED SUBSET only; :1944-1948 prints engine_only= as a SET DIFFERENCE; and :1969 and :2220 both TRUNCATE the list. cert_sweep_readout._miss_pairs partitions on the literal 'engine' (:111) and _PAIR_RE (:78) matches both renderings, so it silently consumes engine_only= too. The field is not a component set under any reading.

what_is_retracted.c92_entirely: the claim that 1 of 8 remaining limit adjudications survives. Every 'reachable / not reachable' verdict in it was computed by the invalid method. The conclusion may be right or wrong; the evidence cannot support it either way.
what_is_retracted.c89_evidence_table: AS ORIGINALLY WRITTEN. the_deciding_check.result was wrong: for 19000074/27 the engine DOES emit an arm reaching the observed net -244 -- the 1.56% C27 crit-kill arm. 'ABSENT in all four' is false; it is absent in three. Already corrected on PR #1031, which now reads 'CORRECTED. Absent in THREE of four' and cites this report. reports/c89 does not exist on main.
what_is_retracted.c89_conclusion_partially_survives: for 19000029/51, 19000052/36 and 19000058/19 the observed nets (-116, -182, -120 on replay) are genuinely absent from the branch sets, so the residual-decided-lethality mechanism stands for three rows. 19000074/27 needs re-adjudication: its arm reaches the right net but still differs on the OTHER slot, which is a different mechanism.

what_is_NOT_affected.SCOPE_WARNING: an earlier draft of this key was an affirmative all-clear and was wrong by omission. Review found further artifacts and two LIVE CLASSIFIER CODE PATHS making the same 'what does this arm contain' claim. The survey below replaces it.
what_is_NOT_affected.c91: STANDS. Its finding -- 15 of 24 limit rows closed by the C88-A matcher fix -- was measured by sweeping before and after, not by reading miss strings.
what_is_NOT_affected.c87_c88A_c90: unaffected. C87 and C88-A were measured by sweep; C90 was read from the two sources directly.
what_is_NOT_affected.c93: STANDS, and has since been CONFIRMED BY REPLAY -- see the REPLAY_CONFIRMATION block in reports/c93_crit_tag_renderer_gap.json. An earlier draft of this file said C93's 'the crit arm IS present' claim still needed the replay check; that check has been done and the claim held.

the_correct_method: scripts/replay_residue.py re-derives each branch's full component set against the vendored engine. Any claim about what an engine arm CONTAINS must come from replay, never from branch_misses. branch_misses answers 'why did this branch fail', not 'what did this branch do'.
why_this_matters_beyond_the_two_reports: This is the same failure the ledger keeps recording: building a cheap proxy for a question and reading its output as the answer. branch_misses is a diagnostic log, and I used it as a data structure. It was consistently wrong rather than randomly wrong, which is why nothing caught it -- the zero arms looked like plausible miss arms.
action: c92's conclusion is withdrawn pending a replay-based re-test. The 7 rows it moved back to 'open' return to their prior state: filed as limits, adjudication UNVERIFIED rather than falsified.

evidence_path.note: replay prints BOTH slots' full component sets for every branch, which is the field branch_misses does not provide.

This is the phantom-zero arm verbatim. Replay (reports/c96) shows those arms are NOT empty of instructions: they are voided by the renderer's segment() returning None.

scripts/family_bucket_audit.py.status: LIVE CODE PATH computing a published adjudication from miss strings.
scripts/family_bucket_audit.py.where: signatures() at :164-185 -- :171 calls readout._miss_pairs(majority), then :181-185 does net_identical = sum(observed) == sum(engine).
scripts/family_bucket_audit.py.why_it_is_the_same_error: that is a WHOLE-BOUNDARY net computed from ONE SLOT's partial, roll-scaled, possibly truncated list.
scripts/family_bucket_audit.py.the_code_warned_about_this: its own comment at :179-180 says this is the ONLY signature bucket_from_signatures treats as decisive, 'so a false positive here becomes a published adjudication'.
scripts/family_bucket_audit.py.what_it_published: reports/c68_family_bucket_audit.json:66 -- '120/120 majority arms reach an IDENTICAL net HP: the end states agree' -- republished as a current-era ADJUDICATED verdict at reports/c86:58-60, which is the I4_attribution_tie instrument-artifact bucket (3 live rows).
scripts/family_bucket_audit.py.independent_outcome: reports/c95 re-derived I4 from replay and found the nets ARE identical (a Liquid Ooze heal mislabelled as leechseed rather than itemleftovers). So the I4 VERDICT survives on replay evidence -- but it survives by luck of the method, not because of it, and the audit script must be re-based on replay before it adjudicates anything else.

scripts/cert_sweep_readout.py.mitigation: fires 0 rows in the 39-row residue, so nothing currently rests on it. It must still be re-based on replay before it is relied on.

standing_rule: ANY claim about what an engine arm CONTAINS comes from scripts/replay_residue.py, never from branch_misses. branch_misses answers 'why did this branch fail', not 'what did this branch do'. Recorded in docs/engine_divergence_ledger_20260728.md so it is findable outside the retraction that caused it.
record_left_inconsistent_on_main: limit:roll_divergent_lethality is now asserted four ways on main: adjudicated and era_current (c86:18-23), falsified for 15 rows (c91), 7-of-8 failing (c92, now retracted), and unverified (this report). c86 and c92 both carry pointers to this file as of this commit; the family's true status is UNVERIFIED pending a replay-based re-test.
